From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: EdgeScale Ops <gpuops@edgescale.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserve runway & weekly fleet ops: forecast-to-reserve alignment

Team / Aisha —

Following up from last week’s pipeline readout: Neptune looks like it will cross our Dedicated threshold in Q4 assuming the midpoint close cadence. I attached the latest reserve_runway_modeling_v2.xlsx and a heatmap for quick reference.

Ask: can we confirm the delta (GPU weeks) between the current committed Dedicated capacity and the forecasted peak for HS-4472 by EOD Thursday so finance can do an approval pass? Specifics below:

- Sales (Ben/Laura): confirm expected monthly token run-rate scenarios (base/mid/accelerated) and date ranges for ramp windows.
- Infra (Karthik): estimate timelines to provision additional reserved slots vs burst credits, plus any minimum lead times for GPU procurement or partner burst (EdgeScale).
- Finance (Monica): need a ballpark cost delta and the approval path (PO vs contract amendment) if run-rate exceeds committed tiers.

Key constraints: we want to avoid over-committing GPUs that block other deals while ensuring Neptune’s latency SLOs are met. Consider quantization or model-splitting as cost mitigations in the infra estimate.

Next checkpoint: weekly ops sync on Friday at 10am PT if we have numbers; otherwise I’ll push for an interim 30-min call.

Attachments: reserve_runway_modeling_v2.xlsx (workbook, capacity scenarios), deal_heatmap_07_18.pdf (visual summary)

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Sales Ops & Capacity

Rishi —

Quick numbers from Sales triple-checking the deal book: Neptune (HS-4472) midpoint assumes 120M tokens/month by Nov and 220M tokens/month by Jan (accelerated). Close probability is 65% for Oct window, 80% by Jan if we hit the next two milestones.

Notes: their technical team explicitly called out low tail-latency for streaming inference; they will not accept >200ms p50 on the primary path. They asked about burst-to-dedicated migration if they scale faster.

I updated the Scenario tab in your workbook with base/mid/accel rows and a short narrative. See row highlights.

Ben

Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserve runway & weekly fleet ops: forecast-to-reserve alignment

Folks —

Infra readout after running the scenarios:

- Committed delta (midpoint Nov): ~18 GPU-weeks/month (NVIDIA A800 equiv) to meet sustained throughput with current model profile.
- Accelerated (Jan peak): ~32 GPU-weeks/month.
- Lead times: if we do internal reserved pools, procurement + provisioning = ~6–8 weeks. Partner burst (EdgeScale) can cover up to 50% of peak within 10 business days, but requires a short-term connectivity and pricing addendum.

Mitigations/options:
- Quantized variant: estimated 20–25% GPU savings but needs a short quality check with Neptune (2–3 days).
- Model-splitting (streaming + batched path): preserves p50 latency, reduces token cost at tail but increases infra orchestration complexity.

I pinged EdgeScale (cc'd) to check instant availability and pricing floor for a 12-week bridge. EdgeScale, can you confirm availability and a rough $/GPU-hour?

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserve runway & weekly fleet ops: forecast-to-reserve alignment

Team —

Finance notes and immediate needs:

- Cost delta: using Karthik's midpoint (18 GPU-weeks/month) and our unit economics, incremental run-rate is approximately $128k/month on top of current commitment (assuming on-demand partner pricing for the first 12 weeks, then amortized reserved pricing thereafter).
- Approval path: for an uptick under $150k/month we can handle via PO amendment under existing contract; above that we need CFO sign-off + legal to add an amendment.
- Ask: please update the workbook with two cost rows — Partner-burst-first-12-weeks and Reserved-commit-after-12-weeks — so I can produce a short memo for procurement.

If Neptune accepts a short quality guardrail (quantized model), we can shave ~25% from those numbers — please flag in the workbook if we want that option priced.

Monica
Monica Patel
Finance Manager, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good progress. Short summary and action items: 

1) Ben/Laura: finalize Neptune ramp commitment (select base/mid/accel) and confirm whether they'll accept a 2–3 day quantized validation by Monday EOD. Update Scenario tab (Ben updated but please finalize) — due Mon 07/23 EOD.
2) Karthik: confirm EdgeScale availability + $/GPU-hour and a statement of work for 12-week bridge by Mon 07/23 EOD. If EdgeScale can’t cover >50% we’ll plan a partial reserved commit (6–8 week lead).
3) Monica: prepare PO amendment draft for up to $150k/month and a CFO escalation template if we exceed that. Draft due Tue 07/24.
4) Ops sync: keep Friday 10am PT as the rolling weekly checkpoint; if Ben confirms accelerated scenario we'll move to a midweek bridge call.

I’ll circulate a one-pager (pulling numbers from the workbook) for procurement and attach to the HubSpot deal record. Thanks for the quick turn.

Rishi
